page.layout: One page of text in verse with italic mottoes and headings; a manuscript Greek annotation in the lower margin left; a bracket beside lines; a handwritten Greek note at the foot (not printed, so not transcribed). Running head at top; page number 120 at top left.

main_text.l: Viuida tum coelo surgent suspiria: tumque
Quaesitum tangent feruida vota polum.

l.i: Non medicus, sed morbus causa mali. Peccatum

main_text.l: Vis ferri flammaeque secat quod putria membra,
Non medicus, verum morbus id acer agit.
Vastatas urbes ferro quod cernis & igne,
Peccatum causa est, culpa nec vlla Dei.
Evolat, aduerso mutatus frigore, feruor,
Fornacis clausae sint nisi saepe fores.
Sic mens, quae laxo nimium blaterauerit ore,
Diffluit, & constat vix bene firma sibi.
Non potes oculo bene cernere, si vaga currant
Lumina, nec fixo stent requieta loco.
Sic vaga mens mundi curā distracta fugacis,
Non vlla verum cernere parte potest.
Parua lacus magni fundum scintilla subintrans,
Articulo minimo temporis obruitur.
Tristitiae molem terrenae gaudia caeli
Absorbent nullo deperitura die.

l.i: Aqua iactu lapidis turbida. Mens duris

main_text.l: Si lapis in vitream coniectus decidit vndam,
Turbatur motae splendor amoenus aquae.
In pa-

page.notes: Printed text is partly damaged and faded at the right and left edges; some letters are uncertain. A handwritten Greek annotation at the foot and manuscript marks are not transcribed. The bracket at left marks the Tristitia emblem. The catchword "In pa-" is treated as a foot line.
